Bocki New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Boćki, Poland

Demolished. Boćki, first mentioned in the late 15th century and granted town rights around 1513 as a private town, was twice destroyed in the mid-17th century wars and again in 1769, rebuilt by the early 18th century. Jews received settlement permission from the Sapieha family in 1568; population reached 666 by the end of the 18th century, peaking at 66% (1,262) by 1878 before settling around 800 (30%) by 1939. Germany occupied the town in June 1941, establishing a ghetto that fall; October deportations sent residents to Treblinka. This newer cemetery, likely established at the end of the 19th century, held execution victims during WWII, with additional remains exhumed from elsewhere and reburied there afterward; German forces removed matzevot for construction, and local residents continued the theft postwar.
